item.title: US eyes Iran as possible culprit in dozens of new cyberattacks against ships, WSJ reports
item.description:
Nov 23 (Reuters) - The United States is investigating Iran's potential involvement in dozens of cyberattacks against energy tankers amid concerns that Tehran is widening the war with cyber operations and terror plots against Americans far from the Middle East, the Wall Street Journal reported on Monday.

As many as 50 ships carrying oil, liquefied petroleum, chemical products and other explosive substances are believed to have been attacked, the Journal said, citing US officials and others familiar with the matter.

item.title: Iran carries out flogging of singer and her team, Iranian website says
item.description:
DUBAI, Nov 23 (Reuters) - An Iranian singer and four members of her production team have each received 74 lashes after being sentenced for "offending public decency by producing and publishing obscene and immoral content online", an Iranian news website said on Monday.

Parastoo Ahmadi and the four others were also handed two-year bans on artistic and musical activities and travel, the Emtedad website quoted lawyer Mostafa Nili as saying.

item.title: US imposes sanctions on dozens linked to Iran's shadow banking networks
item.description:
By Andrea Shalal

WASHINGTON, Nov 23 (Reuters) - The Trump administration has issued new Iran-related sanctions targeting dozens of people and entities, the Treasury Department said on Monday, stepping up its effort to isolate Iran from the global economy and disrupt its shadow banking networks.

Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) also released an analysis identifying nearly $15 billion of financial activity conducted from January 2025 to August 2026 that it said was potentially linked to Iranian shadow banking.

item.title: Turkey's Erdogan says COP31 laid groundwork for more climate talks despite lack of deal
item.description:
ANKARA, Nov 23 (Reuters) - Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan said on Monday that the COP31 climate summit held in Turkey had established a valuable foundation for future negotiations, even though countries failed to reach consensus on a final deal, known as a cover decision.

"It would have been better if agreement had also been reached on the cover decision on the final day. Nevertheless, a very valuable foundation has been established for the next round of negotiations," Erdogan said, speaking after a cabinet meeting.
